we introduce a facile method for the rapid fabrication and assembly of microfluidic components, which can be easily integrated into microfluidic systems.
we present a facile, cost-efficient, and rapid method of fabricating microtubes for 2D or 3D microsystems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and applications of microtubes for microfluidic systems.
the development of a new microfabrication approach for rapid, low-cost, scalable, and modular construction of soft microtubes.
the development of a novel microfluidic technology that is simple, low-cost, rapid, and modular, and thus, can be widely used for a variety of applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a facile method to fabricate microtubes for the rapid construction, reconfiguration, and reiteration of various microfluidic systems.
the proposed method provides a facile, low cost, and efficient method for fabricating soft, elastomeric microtube devices for a variety of applications in the field of microfluidics.
the presented soft tubular microfabrication method provides a facile and low-cost alternative for microfluidic device fabrication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current cleanroom-based fabrication process is expensive and complicated, which limits the development of microfluidic technology.
we introduce a facile method to rapidly fabricate soft, elastic, and biocompatible microtubes.
soft tubular microtubes provide an alternative solution for rapid prototyping of functional microfluidic devices, without compromising their performance, functionality, and precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated a simple, rapid, and low-cost approach of fabricating elastomer microtubes for microfluidics applications.
we demonstrate how soft tubular microtubes can serve as the basic building block for the rapid construction and reconfigurations of microfluidic systems.
we demonstrate how microfluidic devices can be fabricated without cleanroom facilities and can be assembled into 3D structures with complex topologies.
